model_design_implications.key_insight: Category alone is a WEAK signal. The model needs to score on DRAMA + NOVELTY + PERSONAL_IMPACT, not just topic match. Same category can be 5 or 1 depending on the story's nature.
features_needed: drama_score: How dramatic/consequential is this event? (Kent resignation = high, market up 0.2% = low)
novelty_score: Is this a FIRST or BREAKTHROUGH? (Salah 50th CL goal = high, Procore integration = low)
personal_impact: Does this affect the user's daily life, career, or identity? (Egypt fuel hike = high, One Piece = zero)
conversation_worthy: Would the user want to discuss this? (Ohio meteor = yes, Mistral Small 4 = no)
follow_list_match: Does this involve a person/entity the user explicitly follows? (Sam Altman = yes, Mistral = no)
calendar_awareness: Hijri calendar, Egyptian holidays, company events
anti_patterns: Don't over-index on category. Finance = 5 (when it's dramatic) or hidden (when it's routine numbers)
Don't equate 'employer' with 'industry'. Procore news ≠ construction tech innovation
Don't limit geopolitics geographically. Cuba got higher stars than some Iran stories
Don't filter entertainment by genre similarity. The Office ≠ Peaky Blinders even though both are 'TV'
